outcomes.label: response_control

modifiers: Resposta específica ao regime de radiação

Resposta à presença de comorbidades (HAS, hipotireoidismo)

outcomes.label: persistence

outcomes.mechanism: Falha da radioterapia em controlar a doença metastática pulmonar.
modifiers: Resistência molecular ou biológica do tumor
Progressão da doença metastática durante o período de tratamento
Impacto da condição funcional e toxicidade da radioterapia

outcomes.label: recurrence_progression
outcomes.description: Recorrência ou progressão da doença local ou metastática após a Radioterapia Externa (DTC_EBRT).
outcomes.mechanism: Falha do controle locorregional ou progressão da doença metastática.

outcomes.label: toxicity
outcomes.description: Ocorrência de toxicidade relacionada à Radioterapia Externa (DTC_EBRT).
outcomes.mechanism: Efeitos adversos da irradiação externa.

Estado geral de saúde do paciente

outcomes.label: quality_of_life

outcomes.mechanism: Impacto da doença residual, toxicidade e condições de saúde concomitantes.

outcomes.label: subsequent_therapy

modifiers: Grau de controle alcançado pela DTC_EBRT

outcomes.label: mortality
outcomes.description: Mortalidade geral do paciente.
outcomes.mechanism: Evolução da doença e impacto da toxicidade/comorbidades.
modifiers: Mortalidade basal relacionada à doença e comorbidades

Evidence Quality Assessment The quality of evidence was assessed for each outcome of interest. This rating includes factors such as study design, consistency of results, directness of evidence, precision, publication bias, and magnitude of effect, assessed by one reviewer. Evidence quality ratings for the outcomes of in- terest are provided in the supplement. Refer to Appendix Table A2 for deﬁnitions for the quality of the evidence, and the Methodology Manual for more information. RECOMMENDATIONS All recommendations are available in Table 2, a n d Figures 1-4 show the recommendations as algorithms. WELL-DIFFERENTIATED The primary treatment of well-differentiated thyroid cancer is surgery with or without radioactive iodine (RAI) therapy. In the event of recurrence, multidisciplinary management of these cases is recommended, including evaluation for further therapy with surgery, RAI, and/or external-beam radiotherapy.

impacts.impact: Risco de disfagia (dificuldade para engolir) durante o tratamento com radioterapia externa, uma toxicidade potencial da radioterapia.
Possibilidade de dermatite (irritação/inflamação da pele) associada à radioterapia externa.
Impacto na qualidade de vida devido à progressão da doença (radiological progression documented on serial CT) e doença metastática em pulmões.

rationale: A progressão radiológica após a radioterapia externa pode ser causada pela inadequação da dose de radiação para controlar a doença localmente avançada.
A progressão da doença metastática pulmonar é resultado da resistência da doença ao controle locorregional após a radioterapia.
A progressão radiológica do câncer de tireoide, apesar do tratamento prévio, é causada pela falha do controle locorregional devido à inadequação da dose ou conformidade da radioterapia externa.
A intolerância à radioterapia externa (DTC_EBRT) foi causada pela toxicidade potencial da radiação sobre o tecido tireoidiano remanescente ou estruturas adjacentes.
A falha do controle locorregional após a radioterapia externa é causada pela inadequação da dose de radiação para atingir o tumor residual.
A progressão metastática pulmonar é resultado da resistência da doença ao tratamento prévio com iodo radioativo.
A baixa atividade de iodo radioativo nas metástases pulmonares permitiu a progressão da doença apesar da radioterapia, indicando resistência ao controle locorregional.
A presença de doença metastática pulmonar, combinada com o perfil molecular BRAF V600E positivo, levou à falha do controle locorregional.
A progressão radiológica do carcinoma de tireoide (pT3b pN1b cM1) levou à necessidade de radioterapia externa, que foi interrompida devido à intolerância.
A comorbidade de hipertensão arterial e hipotireoidismo pós-tireoidectomia afetou a tolerância do paciente à radioterapia externa.
A doença metastática pulmonar radioiodina-refractária impediu o controle locorregional, levando à progressão apesar da radioterapia externa.

external_evidence.finding: The results of the prospective randomized trials conﬁrm that MKI leads to improved PFS compared to placebo for ﬁrst-line RAI-refractory DTC, and likely also provide beneﬁt in patients with PDTC or DHGTC. In particular, lenvatinib has a moderate quality of evidence supporting its use, given more impressive PFS beneﬁt compared to sorafenib or vandetanib. Thus, for patients with driver mutation–negative PDTC or DHGTC with RAI-refractory and progressive disease re- quiring systemic therapy, lenvatinib or sorafenib may be considered. Lenvatinib with pembrolizumab may be con- sidered for patients with aggressive PDTC or DHGTC, but there is insufﬁcient evidence to formally recommend this strategy. Recommendation 5.2 Literature review and analysis. The literature review did not yield any prospective or retrospective studies of MKI in the subsequent-line setting speciﬁcally for PDTC or DHGTC. COSMIC-311, 73 which established cabozantinib as second- line therapy, RAI-refractory, differentiated thyroid cancer, included fewer than 10 patients with PDTC and thus did not meet criteria for inclusion as part of the evidence base for this guideline. Clinical interpretation.

external_evidence.finding: The results of the prospective randomized trials conﬁrm that MKI leads to improved PFS compared to placebo for ﬁrst-line RAI-refractory DTC, and likely also provide beneﬁt in patients with PDTC or DHGTC. In particular, lenvatinib has a moderate quality of evidence supporting its use, given more impressive PFS beneﬁt compared to sorafenib or vandetanib. Thus, for patients with driver mutation–negative PDTC or DHGTC with RAI-refractory and progressive disease re- quiring systemic therapy, lenvatinib or sorafenib may be considered. Lenvatinib with pembrolizumab may be con- sidered for patients with aggressive PDTC or DHGTC, but there is insufﬁcient evidence to formally recommend this strategy. Recommendation 5.2 Literature review and analysis. The literature review did not yield any prospective or retrospective studies of MKI in the subsequent-line setting speciﬁcally for PDTC or DHGTC. COSMIC-311, 73 which established cabozantinib as second- line therapy, RAI-refractory, differentiated thyroid cancer, included fewer than 10 patients with PDTC and thus did not meet criteria for inclusion as part of the evidence base for this guideline. Clinical interpretation.

impacts.impact: Risco de eventos cardiovasculares devido à comorbidade de hipertensão arterial e ao uso de inibidores de quinase sistêmicos.
Fadiga e alterações na qualidade de vida relacionadas à terapia sistêmica.
Possível piora da função renal devido à toxicidade potencial do tratamento.

rationale: A progressão radiológica do câncer de tireoide, com mutação BRAF_V600E positiva, induziu uma falha na resposta ao tratamento prévio (ablação com I-131), tornando a doença refratária ao radioiodo.
A toxicidade do tratamento sistêmico foi causada pela progressão da doença metastática refratária ao iodo.
A intolerância ao DTC_RAIRD_MKI foi causada pela progressão radiológica documentada do câncer.
A interação entre a hipertensão arterial e o hipotireoidismo pós-tireoidectomia comprometeu a capacidade funcional do paciente para tolerar a terapia sistêmica.

external_evidence.finding: best practices for prevention, screening, palliative and supportive care, and disease management of cancer. In the United States, many patients remain unable to reap the beneﬁts of innovative prevention and early detection programs, biomarker testing, and new cancer therapies due to challenges including lack of transportation, stable housing, adequate insurance coverage, food insecurity, health literacy, proximity to a dedicated cancer center, and cost of treatment and other services. 94 Additionally, some populations experience stigma along with barriers to cancer screening, prevention, and treatment that contribute to these cancer disparities. 95 Further, geographic disparities can also impact the quality- of-care patients receive. Rural patients are more likely to have worse survivorship outcomes and experience higher mortality rates compared to nonrural patients. This can be attributed, in part, to a lower density of specialists and dedicated cancer centers, as only 21% of nonmetropolitan counties in the United States have one or more practicing oncologists.
external_evidence.relevance: 4 termos da consulta correspondem ao trecho.

external_evidence.finding: Furthermore, access to the necessary systemic therapy medications, including MKIs, may vary based on treatment location. Finally, many thyroid malignancies are rare; expertise in management is not universal and may impact care. Overall, there is signiﬁcant opportunity to improve access to swift diagnosis, high-quality pathological diagnosis, and expertise in multidisciplinary treatment of thyroid carci- nomas to improve patient care. MULTIPLE CHRONIC CONDITIONS Creating evidence-based recommendations to inform treat- ment of patients with additional chronic conditions, a situa- tion in which the patient may have two or more such conditions—referred to as multiple chronic conditions (MCC)—is challenging. Patients with MCC are a complex and heterogeneous population, making it difﬁcult to account for all of the possible permutations to develop speciﬁc recommen- dations for care. In addition, the best available evidence for treating index conditions, such as cancer, is often from clinical trials whose study selection criteria may exclude these patients in order to avoid potential interaction effects or confounding of results associated with MCC.

In the United States, many patients remain unable to reap the beneﬁts of innovative prevention and early detection programs, biomarker testing, and new cancer therapies due to challenges including lack of transportation, stable housing, adequate insurance coverage, food insecurity, health literacy, proximity to a dedicated cancer center, and cost of treatment and other services. 94 Additionally, some populations experience stigma along with barriers to cancer screening, prevention, and treatment that contribute to these cancer disparities. 95 Further, geographic disparities can also impact the quality- of-care patients receive. Rural patients are more likely to have worse survivorship outcomes and experience higher mortality rates compared to nonrural patients. This can be attributed, in part, to a lower density of specialists and dedicated cancer centers, as only 21% of nonmetropolitan counties in the United States have one or more practicing oncologists.

external_evidence.finding: Furthermore, access to the necessary systemic therapy medications, including MKIs, may vary based on treatment location. Finally, many thyroid malignancies are rare; expertise in management is not universal and may impact care. Overall, there is signiﬁcant opportunity to improve access to swift diagnosis, high-quality pathological diagnosis, and expertise in multidisciplinary treatment of thyroid carci- nomas to improve patient care. MULTIPLE CHRONIC CONDITIONS Creating evidence-based recommendations to inform treat- ment of patients with additional chronic conditions, a situa- tion in which the patient may have two or more such conditions—referred to as multiple chronic conditions (MCC)—is challenging. Patients with MCC are a complex and heterogeneous population, making it difﬁcult to account for all of the possible permutations to develop speciﬁc recommen- dations for care. In addition, the best available evidence for treating index conditions, such as cancer, is often from clinical trials whose study selection criteria may exclude these patients in order to avoid potential interaction effects or confounding of results associated with MCC.

impacts.impact: Risco de fadiga ou dispneia ao realizar esforços físicos, dado o histórico de dispneia aos grandes esforços.
Impacto na qualidade de vida relacionado ao manejo da hipertensão arterial e hipotireoidismo pós-tireoidectomia.
Preocupação com a progressão da doença metastática (pulmão) e o risco de recorrência elevada.

rationale: A baixa avidez ao iodo radioativo das metástases pulmonares levou à falha na resposta à terapia de iodo radioativo, resultando em progressão da doença.
A progressão radiológica do câncer de tireoide, apesar do status molecular BRAF_V600E positivo, é causada pela ineficácia da terapia prévia (ablação com I-131) contra a doença metastática pulmonar.
A hipotireoidismo pós-tireoidectomia e a hipertensão arterial contribuem para a progressão do câncer, limitando a resposta tecidual à terapia.
A progressão radiológica do câncer de tireoide, associada a metástases pulmonares radioiodine-refractórias, leva à intolerância ao tratamento de suporte.
A progressão radiológica do câncer de tireoide é causada pela ineficácia da ablação com I-131 prévia contra as metástases pulmonares.
A progressão radiológica do carcinoma papilífero, com metástases pulmonares radioiodine-refractórias, causa dispneia aos grandes esforços.
A comorbidade de hipertensão arterial e o hipotireoidismo pós-tireoidectomia agravam a resposta fisiológica à progressão tumoral.
